text.p: These are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- The 1997 budget proposal set government spending at 737.9 billion tolars ($4.4 billion), 24 percent higher than in 1996.
- The centre-left Liberal Democrats and the conservative People's Party signed an annex to their February coalition agreement in which they detailed relations between the two parties.
- Heavy rain on Tuesday caused a lot of damange in Senozece, a city west of Ljubljana.
- The new takeover bill became law on Tuesday after parliament passed it for the second time, overruling the upper house's veto.
- Slovenia's only port Luka Koper expects its cargo traffic to rise by 30 percent this year.

- Civil society group "December 23rd" made its sixth attempt to file for a referendum on whether Slovenia should allow foreigners to buy real estate. Parliament turned down all previous referendum initiatives citing irregular administration proceedings on the group's part.
- A month-long summer festival featuring local and foreign music, dancing and theatre groups, started in Ljubljana on Tuesday.
- State-owned bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka is expected to buy into Slovenian insurer Concordia. Concordia is looking for fresh investors and plans to enlarge its capital by the end of the year.
